stories.title: Shoegaze Music Discovery
stories.description: Amit shares his recent discovery of the 'Shoegaze' genre via Spotify recommendations, tracing his journey from Yo La Tengo to Galaxie 500 and Luna, and explaining the genre's name (guitarists looking at their shoes/pedals).

stories.title: Boris and Igor's Goat
stories.description: Ajay recounts a story from Steven Pinker about two Russian farmers. When Igor sees Boris has a goat, he doesn't want a goat for himself; he wants Boris's goat killed. This illustrates the destructive nature of focusing on inequality rather than poverty.

stories.title: The Matunga Racket
stories.description: Amit describes a past racket in Mumbai where police would entrap gay men (when homosexuality was illegal) at Matunga railway station and extort them, illustrating the harms of criminalizing victimless acts.

stories.title: Child Labor in Bangladesh and Nepal
stories.description: Amit cites studies showing that when Western activists successfully campaigned to ban child labor in sweatshops, many of the displaced children ended up in worse situations like prostitution or crime, highlighting the unintended consequences of 'luxury beliefs'.

stories.title: The Single Malt Socialist
stories.description: Amit describes meeting a successful professional at a party who advocated for 'degrowth' while sipping single malt whiskey, pointing out the hypocrisy and immorality of such a stance for a developing country.

recommendations.item: Troubled: A Memoir of Foster Care, Family, and the Future of Social Class
recommendations.comment: Rob Henderson's memoir, which introduces the concept of 'luxury beliefs'.
Steven Pinker's book, the source of the Boris and Igor story.
Harry Frankfurt's book arguing for the 'doctrine of sufficiency' over equality.
Walter Block's controversial book defending despised figures like the pimp and the slumlord.
Thomas Sowell's book on the self-congratulatory nature of social policy.
Album by Galaxie 500, recommended by Amit.

core_ideas.description: Ideas and opinions that confer status on the upper class while inflicting costs on the lower classes (e.g., defunding the police, opposing sweatshops from afar).
The distinction that poverty is the real problem to be solved (via growth), while inequality is a secondary concern that, if targeted wrongly (killing Boris's goat), can lead to universal poverty.
The argument that banning acts between consenting adults (prostitution, betting, drug use) creates black markets, empowers the underworld, and increases harm/coercion.
The trendy disdain for capitalism and growth (degrowth) among the elite, which ignores that growth is the only proven way to lift masses out of poverty.
The economic fallacy that capping prices helps the poor; in reality, it destroys incentives to produce, leads to shortages, and creates black markets.
The tendency to hold beliefs that make one feel good or look good to one's tribe, rather than doing the hard work of understanding what actually helps people.
